nodes.label: Build once, promote always
nodes.rationale: Rebuilding per environment invites "works in staging" drift; the artifact that passed main verification should be the same bytes deployed to every downstream environment.

nodes.label: Three-layer pipeline model (PR / main / release)
nodes.rationale: Separating PR validation, main/trunk verification, and release/promotion makes the separation of concerns visible even when layers share a file, and keeps the build-once/promote-always discipline enforceable.

nodes.label: Trunk-based development default
nodes.rationale: Short-lived PR branches merged to a single mainline are preferred over long-lived GitFlow release branches, consistent with DORA-oriented delivery research and most modern CI designs.

nodes.label: Least-privilege workflow permissions
nodes.rationale: Set a workflow-level read-only permissions floor and grant write scopes only on the specific jobs that need them, so a compromised step cannot push code, mint releases, or change settings.

nodes.label: Blocking vs advisory gates
nodes.rationale: Rolling a new scanner out as advisory first is fine; leaving it advisory forever without a plan is a finding at standard+ maturity — required status checks should match the blocking set.

nodes.label: Determinism-First Principle
nodes.rationale: When a task can be solved with deterministic code, prefer that over an LLM call; reserve the LLM for genuinely ambiguous/unstructured reasoning. Generalized from VSIP's principle #5. Only a live design choice when the project has an LLM/agent component.

nodes.label: Agent Harness
nodes.rationale: The engineered layer around a bare model call (loop, tool interfaces, context/memory, permissions, observability) that turns it into bounded, stateful, tool-mediated task execution. The model is a replaceable component behind it.

nodes.label: LLM/Agent-Specific Principles
nodes.rationale: Parent family (harness, model-switching, provenance, relevance+confidence) flagged inapplicable for any project without an LLM/agent component.

nodes.label: Model-Switching Capability
nodes.rationale: A well-built harness lets the underlying model change, even mid-session, without restructuring the system; practical test is whether switching needs a restart.

nodes.label: Provenance (Evidence Tracing)
nodes.rationale: Ability to trace a generated claim/action back to the specific evidence that produced it, distinct from citation (display). Guards against post-rationalized citations. Recording is architectural; surfacing to the user is a UX decision.

nodes.label: Relevance/Confidence Scoring
nodes.rationale: Paired with provenance: a source without a relevance/confidence signal doesn't tell the consumer how much to trust it. No universal confidence threshold exists; a domain-specific calibration set is recommended, with 0.7+/0.5+ precision@k as an illustrative anchor.

nodes.label: LLM/Agent-Component Detection Decision (#1)
nodes.rationale: Ask explicitly during inception, captured in the baseline record, and re-checked on every audit-mode invocation; drift in either direction updates the record and applies/retires the conditional LLM-specific principles section.

nodes.rationale: Red-green-refactor loop; forces designing the interface before the implementation, pushing toward decoupled modular design. AI-assisted development does not change the core discipline.

nodes.label: Testability
nodes.rationale: The architecture must have seams where a real dependency can be substituted for a fake/mock, or verification of any kind is structurally blocked. The structural precondition TDD depends on.

nodes.label: Architecture Pattern Selection Heuristic
nodes.rationale: Decision framework connecting project answers (team size, scale, latency/consistency, compliance, domain complexity, deployment constraints) to a recommended pattern; anchored on Azure's style x dependency-management x domain table plus Fowler's monolith-first heuristic.

nodes.label: Software vs Non-Software Top-Level Fork (#3)

nodes.label: ajv
nodes.rationale: Raw JSON-Schema-standard validation, the right choice for cross-language schema portability or when raw validation throughput matters more than TS-inference ergonomics; also the engine underneath env-schema.

nodes.label: convict
nodes.rationale: Node-ecosystem analog of pydantic-settings' typed layer: schema-validated nested config, originated at Mozilla; the more established of the two typed-config npm options.

nodes.label: dynaconf
nodes.rationale: Layered, multi-environment config files rather than a single flat env-var-to-field mapping; the right choice for genuinely different config files per environment.

nodes.label: env-schema
nodes.rationale: Validated env-var config expressed as JSON Schema validated via Ajv, plus Node's built-in parseEnv; a narrower, more modern-tooling-aligned option than convict's bespoke DSL.

nodes.label: io-ts (superseded)
nodes.rationale: Historically fp-ts-style Either-based runtime type decoding; not recommended for new projects, last push 2024-12-10 yet still pulls 2.73M/week, the same legacy-inertia pattern as setuptools/bump2version/backoff.

nodes.label: msgspec
nodes.rationale: Narrower performance-focused alternative to pydantic for hot-path throughput when the fuller validation feature set isn't needed; its own benchmark page 404'd this pass, not independently verified.

nodes.label: pydantic-settings
nodes.rationale: The typed layer above dotenv: reads env vars/.env/secrets files into a validated BaseSettings class so malformed values fail fast. Not present in ubi-csr-tmf despite pydantic itself being a direct dependency -- a real, concretely-identified gap.

nodes.label: pydantic v2
nodes.rationale: Declares a data shape once and gets parsing/coercion plus validation for any object crossing a trust boundary. v2's Rust core is a genuine rewrite (~17x speed improvement over v1). ubi-csr-tmf pins pydantic v1, a real upgrade-pressure example given v1 is unsupported on Python 3.14+ and current FastAPI has dropped v1 support.

nodes.label: python-dotenv
nodes.rationale: Loads KEY=value pairs from .env into os.environ for local dev without hand-exporting; real local precedent in ubi-csr-tmf's backend requirements.txt.

nodes.label: zod
nodes.rationale: Define a schema once, get both runtime validation and a compile-time TS type via z.infer, eliminating interface/validator drift. The dominant ergonomics-first npm default.

nodes.label: Reporting Absence as a Finding
nodes.rationale: This domain's distinctive job is reviewing for patterns that don't exist at all and reporting the absence itself as a finding — a codebase with zero resilience patterns scores low even when nothing is actively broken, because the risk is latent until the first outage.

nodes.label: arquero
nodes.rationale: Query processing and transformation of array-backed data tables with real Apache Arrow columnar interop, not just a row-oriented wrapper; from University of Washington's Interactive Data Lab. Pushed 2025-05-29, about 15 months stale relative to this pass.

nodes.label: danfojs
nodes.rationale: Deliberately pandas-shaped API in JavaScript with TensorFlow.js tensor integration; a thinner, less architecturally distinct implementation than arquero, but real recent commit activity.

nodes.label: Dask (scope exclusion)
nodes.rationale: A flexible parallel computing library for analytics -- a distributed/multi-machine cluster computing framework with a pandas-like DataFrame API layered on top; a different axis (multi-node horizontal scale) from every library in this domain's table, deliberately excluded.

nodes.label: DuckDB
nodes.rationale: Embedded, in-process OLAP SQL engine, columnar-vectorized query execution, no server to stand up; can run queries directly on pandas data without importing or copying it. Not a DataFrame-API competitor -- an orthogonal SQL-query layer commonly used together with pandas/Polars.

nodes.label: @duckdb/duckdb-wasm
nodes.rationale: DuckDB itself compiled to WebAssembly, running in-browser or in Node with the same zero-copy Arrow interop; the most architecturally capable and highest-adoption of the three npm candidates researched.

nodes.label: pandas
nodes.rationale: DataFrame backed by NumPy arrays via an internal BlockManager; eager, largely single-core by default. Per pandas' own docs, datasets that are a sizable fraction of memory become unwieldy since some operations make intermediate copies. Correct default when data fits comfortably in memory and the rest of the ecosystem (plotting, ML, notebooks) already assumes a pandas DataFrame. Real local precedent: pinned pandas==2.0.3 in ubi-csr-tmf across five files.

nodes.label: Polars
nodes.rationale: Rust core with multi-threaded, vectorized (SIMD) execution and zero-copy Arrow columnar sharing. Lazy engine applies predicate/projection/slice pushdown, common subplan elimination, and join-order estimation; a streaming engine processes larger-than-memory datasets. Distinct mechanism from pandas, not just a faster reimplementation.

nodes.label: Vaex
nodes.rationale: Memory-maps on-disk files so data is never fully loaded, combined with lazy expression evaluation and a zero-memory-copy policy -- a different mechanism from both pandas (fully in-RAM) and Polars' streaming engine. Core maintainer stepped back (2024); vaex-core still received real if infrequent releases (Sep 2025). Hard current blocker: requires_python <3.13, does not install on Python 3.13/3.14.

nodes.label: CQRS / Event Sourcing
nodes.rationale: Fowler cautions CQRS is appropriate only for complex domains or read/write-disparate high-performance systems; the majority of cases have not been good.

nodes.label: Serverless Architecture
nodes.rationale: Runtime/deployment axis; composes with event-driven rather than competing (e.g. event-driven microservices on serverless compute). Provisioned concurrency costs whether used or not.

nodes.label: Merge Strategy Trade-offs

nodes.label: Monorepo vs Polyrepo Decision

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Records (ADR)
nodes.rationale: Nygard's 2011 format (Title/Status/Context/Decision/Consequences), endorsed by Fowler. Status field supports supersession, important since project-incubation re-audits repos over their lifecycle.

nodes.label: MCPg ADR-0001: Build Approach
nodes.rationale: Local precedent: an 'Options considered' section scored against named criteria, then a Decision stating the choice and why alternatives lost. Marked superseded by ADR-0007 via its Status field.

nodes.label: MCPg ADR-0002: Technology Stack
nodes.rationale: Local precedent: a flat Concern | Choice | Notes decision table plus a 'Deviations from the inherited base' section.

nodes.label: backoff (archived)
nodes.rationale: Historically the same decorator-based retry niche as tenacity; repo is archived (last push 2024-05-02). Not a recommendation for new projects; found pinned alongside tenacity in ubi-csr-tmf, almost certainly transitive pull.

nodes.label: cockatiel
nodes.rationale: Full resilience-policy composition (Retry, Circuit Breaker, Timeout, Bulkhead, Fallback) modeled on .NET's Polly; the genuinely distinct architectural tier above p-retry/tenacity's retry-only scope.

nodes.label: p-retry
nodes.rationale: Retries a promise-returning/async function with exponential backoff; the direct npm analog of tenacity's core use case, part of Sindre Sorhus's p-* family.

nodes.label: pybreaker
nodes.rationale: Python's circuit-breaker answer to cockatiel's npm-side scope; tenacity has no built-in circuit-breaker mode. Typically used together with tenacity, not as a replacement.

nodes.label: tenacity
nodes.rationale: Decorator-based retry for just about anything; composable stop conditions, wait strategies (exponential backoff with jitter), retry-on-exception/return-value predicates. Confirmed still the clear current Python leader.

nodes.label: flydrive
nodes.rationale: Storage-driver abstraction originating in the AdonisJS framework ecosystem, usable standalone; higher npm downloads than flystorage likely from AdonisJS pull-through.

nodes.label: flystorage
nodes.rationale: Same storage-abstraction philosophy as smart_open/fsspec, ported from PHP's Flysystem by the same author (Frank de Jonge); npm's closest conceptual analog, but far below smart_open/fsspec's adoption scale.

nodes.label: fsspec
nodes.rationale: Full filesystem abstraction (ls/glob/cp/rm/mkdir plus open()) across the same backend class; the default many data-tooling libraries (pandas, dask, pyarrow, HF datasets) pull in transitively.

nodes.label: smart_open
nodes.rationale: Drop-in replacement for open() working identically across S3/GCS/Azure Blob/HDFS/SFTP/HTTP(S)/local disk with transparent compression. Default for the user's literal cloud-agnostic storage I/O example; real local-precedent gap in ubi-csr-tmf (which pins boto3/azure-storage SDKs directly with no smart_open/fsspec).

nodes.label: universal_pathlib
nodes.rationale: pathlib.Path-style object API built directly on fsspec's backends, for teams wanting Path idioms extended to cloud paths.

nodes.label: cachetools
nodes.rationale: Adds TTL-based eviction policies (e.g. TTLCache) that stdlib functools.lru_cache structurally cannot express (only pure LRU, no TTL). Real local precedent: pinned directly in ubi-csr-tmf's backend requirements.txt.

nodes.label: diskcache (unmaintained, unpatched CVE)
nodes.rationale: Disk-persisted cache surviving process restarts, not bounded by RAM. Last commit 2024-03-03; carries unpatched moderate-severity CVE-2025-69872 (pickle deserialization RCE via cache-directory write access). Named with a prominent caution, the only real Python disk-persisted local-cache library with meaningful adoption found.

nodes.label: joblib.Memory
nodes.rationale: Disk-caches results of deterministic function calls; a narrower, actively-maintained alternative for the memoize-to-disk sub-case, not a full replacement for diskcache's general key-value cache API.

nodes.label: lru-cache (isaacs/node-lru-cache)
nodes.rationale: Configurable maxSize/sizeCalculation memory-bounded eviction plus TTL for npm; JS has no functools.lru_cache stdlib analog at all. Authored by isaacs (npm's own maintainer).

nodes.label: node-cache
nodes.rationale: Simpler object-literal-style in-memory TTL-only cache; last pushed 2024-06-04, lru-cache outpulls it roughly 105:1 on weekly downloads.

nodes.norm_label: rest vs graphql vs grpc decision table

nodes.label: LWW vs. OT vs. CRDT Conflict Resolution
nodes.norm_label: lww vs. ot vs. crdt conflict resolution

nodes.label: got
nodes.rationale: Full-featured Node HTTP client built on http/https modules with retries, streams, and hooks/interceptors; the richer-featured option for Node-specific (non-browser) code.

nodes.label: httpx
nodes.rationale: Adds native async/await and HTTP/2 while keeping a broadly requests-compatible API; the right choice specifically when calling code is already async.

nodes.label: ky
nodes.rationale: Thin elegant wrapper directly around native fetch adding retries/timeouts/hooks; works in browser and edge runtimes where got's Node-http dependency does not.

nodes.label: requests
nodes.rationale: HTTP for Humans ergonomic wrapper over http.client/urllib; confirmed still the dominant Python default in 2026 (not displaced by httpx), pushed same day as this pass, ~276M downloads/week.

nodes.label: loguru
nodes.rationale: Eliminates stdlib logging's setup boilerplate entirely; the right default for a CLI tool, script, or smaller service wanting near-zero-setup good logging. ~5x structlog's GitHub stars.

nodes.label: pino
nodes.rationale: Performance-first asynchronous minimal-overhead JSON logging for Node; the npm parallel to structlog's machines-first framing.

nodes.label: structlog
nodes.rationale: Logs as key-value/structured data first, designed to emit JSON/logfmt for machine parsing by a log-aggregation pipeline. Higher weekly PyPI downloads than loguru despite far fewer stars, likely heavier transitive-dependency use.

nodes.label: winston
nodes.rationale: Longer-established, more configurable option with multiple simultaneous transports and formats. More stars than pino (pino's parallel to loguru's star lead) but fewer weekly downloads.

nodes.label: APScheduler
nodes.rationale: Cron-style/interval/one-off triggers with a persistent job store, in-process, no broker. Real local precedent in ubi-csr-tmf. Stable 3.x line still actively released; 4.0.0 remains alpha over a year after its last alpha tag, so 3.x is the correct current recommendation.

nodes.label: node-cron
nodes.rationale: Cron-string-driven in-process scheduling, no external daemon needed; the lighter-weight cron-syntax-focused npm option.

nodes.label: node-schedule (stale)
nodes.rationale: Broader scheduling vocabulary (cron plus recurrence rules plus Date-object one-off scheduling) but last pushed 2025-06-19, over a year stale, and pulls fewer weekly downloads than node-cron despite higher star count.

nodes.label: stdlib sched / threading.Timer
nodes.rationale: Zero-dependency floor for a single one-off deferred callback; no cron parsing, persistent job stores, or restart-surviving interval scheduling.

nodes.label: Arrow
nodes.rationale: Friendlier consistent API over stdlib datetime/dateutil with humanized output; per whenever's own README it keeps the same naive/aware footguns as stdlib.

nodes.label: Pendulum
nodes.rationale: Drop-in-feeling stdlib datetime replacement with correct DST-aware arithmetic and a fluent API. Real, verified release-cadence slowdown: only two releases (3.1.0, 3.2.0) between Dec 2023 and this snapshot.

nodes.label: stdlib datetime
nodes.rationale: Zero-dependency baseline; naive-vs-aware comparison raises TypeError only at use time, and arithmetic near a DST boundary can silently produce wrong wall-clock results (stdlib only considers DST across two-timezone calculations).

nodes.label: whenever
nodes.rationale: The only one of the three that fixes both DST-correct arithmetic and type-checker-enforceable naive/aware distinction via distinct types; pre-1.0, API may still change, not yet the default recommendation.

nodes.label: chalk
nodes.rationale: Chainable/nestable terminal string style composition; the npm default for colored terminal text, highest download library in its table by a wide margin.

nodes.label: cli-table3
nodes.rationale: Renders aligned bordered ASCII/Unicode tables; the maintained continuation of the now-stale cli-table.

nodes.label: ora
nodes.rationale: Terminal spinners for long-running async operations with TTY-detection fallback; de facto standard from sindresorhus.

nodes.label: Rich
nodes.rationale: Unifies colored/styled text, tables, markdown, syntax highlighting, progress bars, and pretty-printed data structures under one API; extremely dominant, also the basis for Textual and rich-click.

nodes.label: date-fns
nodes.rationale: Tree-shakeable, purely functional date manipulation; highest current npm download volume of the three date libraries researched. License could not be pinned to a primary-source file this pass.

nodes.label: Day.js
nodes.rationale: Near-drop-in ~2KB Moment.js-API-compatible replacement; pragmatic choice for a Moment-shaped codebase migrating off legacy Moment with minimal rewrite.

nodes.label: Luxon
nodes.rationale: Moment.js team's designated successor; immutable objects plus Intl-backed timezone/locale handling, closer in spirit to the eventual native Temporal API's object model.

nodes.label: Temporal API (TC39)
nodes.rationale: Stage 4 TC39 proposal; Firefox 139, Chrome 144, and Node.js 26 (May 2026) ship it, but MDN flags it as not yet Baseline due to incomplete cross-browser (Safari) support. Not yet safe as the default recommendation for broad browser-runtime compatibility.

nodes.rationale: IaC (Terraform, Pulumi, CloudFormation), Kubernetes/container orchestration, CI/CD platform tooling, internal developer platforms; distinct concerns of idempotency, drift detection, blast-radius limiting, state management. Promoted 2026-08-31 as stack category #7.

nodes.label: ML / AI Model Development Category
nodes.rationale: Training, fine-tuning, experiment tracking, model evaluation; distinct from Data & Analytics Platforms and Agentic & MCP Platforms. RAG-corpus construction resolved to belong to Agentic & MCP Platforms instead. Promoted 2026-08-31 as stack category #8.

nodes.label: MLOps / ML Platform Engineering Category
nodes.rationale: Model registries, feature stores, serving infrastructure, drift monitoring, retraining triggers, canary rollouts for models. Confirmed to stay its own category rather than merge into #1 or #2. Promoted 2026-08-31 as stack category #9.

nodes.label: Security-by-Design
nodes.rationale: Security is a design-time architectural concern, not a pre-launch checklist. Added to the baseline because the user's original list had no explicit security principle.

nodes.label: Cross-Cutting Utility Libraries Batch C
nodes.rationale: Later-added batch researched in response to a direct methodology correction: evaluate by functional/architectural merit first, adoption signals second; pandas vs Polars vs Vaex vs DuckDB named explicitly as the worked example.

nodes.label: factory_boy
nodes.rationale: Declarative Factory classes generating varied test objects with sensible defaults and per-test overrides; the established Python standard for test-data object construction, distinct from Faker's field-value generation.

nodes.label: @faker-js/faker
nodes.rationale: Actively-maintained community-governed successor to the original faker.js, whose author deliberately corrupted/unpublished it in the January 2022 Marak Squires incident. The correct current package to recommend.

nodes.label: Faker (Python)
nodes.rationale: Generates realistic-looking fake field values for test fixtures/seed data; complements factory_boy directly via first-class provider integration.

nodes.label: freezegun (transitioning away from)
nodes.rationale: Still widely-known/historically-dominant time-freezing library; last pushed 2025-08-19 (about a year stale) while still pulling 11.5M/week -- the same legacy-but-still-pulled pattern as diskcache.

nodes.label: @sinonjs/fake-timers
nodes.rationale: The standalone time-mocking engine that also powers Sinon's useFakeTimers(); usable directly without pulling in Sinon's full mocking/stubbing/spying surface.

nodes.label: time-machine
nodes.rationale: Now the currently-preferred Python time-mocking library: faster than freezegun (whose cost is proportional to loaded modules) and finds functions hidden inside arbitrary objects that freezegun misses. Only works with CPython.

nodes.label: Git LFS
nodes.rationale: GitHub's 50MB soft warning / 100MB hard block; practical ceiling of a few hundred MB per file before external object storage or DVC is more appropriate.

nodes.label: Diff-Mode Scope Detection Criterion
nodes.rationale: Tests that a request phrased as 'review my changes against main' is interpreted as diff-mode per SKILL.md routing, and that the review stays scoped to the stated changed file rather than reviewing the whole repo or fabricating findings elsewhere.

nodes.label: Zero Hardcoding / 12-Factor Config
nodes.rationale: Anything that varies between environments must live outside code, in env vars. Litmus test: publishing the repo open source must not leak a secret. Warns against grouping variables into named environment blocks.

nodes.label: Dependency Inversion Principle
nodes.rationale: High-level modules must not depend on low-level modules; both depend on abstractions. Explains why plugin architectures are swappable without touching the core.

nodes.label: Interoperability & Pluggability
nodes.rationale: A system's core should depend on abstractions, not concrete plug-ins; loose coupling, single responsibility per plugin, and a well-defined API are the three load-bearing properties. Seams can be in-process or over-the-wire; the mandate is that seams exist, not a specific mechanism.

nodes.label: Maintainability / Simplicity (KISS, YAGNI, DRY)
nodes.rationale: Default to the simplest design satisfying current known requirements; unnecessary complexity is a direct cost to debuggability, not just aesthetics. These principles alone cannot guarantee production robustness without surrounding architecture/testing/governance.

nodes.label: Scalability & Reliability
nodes.rationale: SRE framing: SLIs roll into SLOs, and an error budget licenses risk-taking vs demanding a stability freeze. Targets are universal (every project should state its target); mechanisms (redundancy, autoscaling, chaos testing) scale with actual stakes.

nodes.label: Spec-Driven Development (SDD)
nodes.rationale: A versioned structured specification is the source of truth AI coding agents build/generate against; a direct response to 'vibe coding' drift and hallucinated APIs. Conditional on AI agents being in the build loop; not yet a universal norm like TDD.

nodes.label: API Design / Versioning Approach
nodes.rationale: Resource-oriented design per Google's AIP-based guide; backward compatibility as the primary goal with versioning as fallback.

nodes.label: Auth Pattern Selection & Secrets Management
nodes.rationale: User-facing -> OAuth2/OIDC; service-to-service -> mTLS or client-credentials; simple partner integration -> API keys, never as sole factor for anything sensitive.

nodes.label: API Gateway vs Service Mesh
nodes.rationale: Gateway (north-south) justified past 1 externally-facing service; mesh (east-west: mTLS, retries, tracing) only past a service-count/maturity threshold most early projects don't cross. Premature mesh adoption is a named anti-pattern.

nodes.label: Kong: API Gateways vs Service Mesh

nodes.label: cross-env (archived)
nodes.rationale: Normalizes Windows vs POSIX env-var syntax in npm scripts to one form. Confirmed fully archived (pushed 2025-11-16), a stronger status than its own README's 'done, maintenance-only' framing; still the practically necessary tool, no live replacement found.

nodes.label: is-ci
nodes.rationale: Single boolean check for whether a process runs inside CI, checking dozens of CI-specific env vars; still genuinely relevant, no stdlib/platform-native equivalent exists.
